blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Generalization to unseen image generators has driven efforts to adapt pretrained visual representations for detection. Yet recent findings show that vision foundation models already encode transferable detection knowledge, while further adaptation can impair generalization. This motivates a shift from backbone adaptation to knowledge readout. Conventional linear probing offers a direct way to read this knowledge but is limited to final-layer RGB features. Multi-cue detectors broaden the evidence base, but their designs introduce other tradeoffs: adaptation may compromise pretrained transferability, heterogeneous encoders complicate feature integration, and late fusion precludes intermediate cross-view interaction. To overcome these limitations, we propose ReMoT, a Mixture-of-Transformers-inspired framework that reads complementary knowledge from spatially aligned RGB and wavelet views within a fully frozen visual foundation. ReMoT employs staged joint attention to enable controlled local and global cross-view interaction, while learnable fusion queries progressively read complementary evidence across Transformer depth without writeback. ReMoT achieves 91.2% average accuracy across eight benchmark groups with 3,074 trainable parameters, attaining the highest overall average among the evaluated methods. These results support structured knowledge readout as a promising alternative to backbone adaptation. Code is available at https://github.com/yunncheng/ReMoT.
blocks.zh: 通俗化到看不见的图像生成器推动了调整预先训练的视觉表现以用于检测的努力。 然而,最近的调查结果表明,愿景基础模型已经编码了可转让检测知识,而进一步调整则会妨碍一般化。 这促使人们从骨干适应转向知识阅读。 常规线性探测为读取这一知识提供了直接途径,但仅限于最后一级RGB特征. 多管探测器拓宽了证据基础,但其设计引入了其他取舍:适应可能损害被预先训练的可转移性,多管编码器使特征集成复杂化,而后聚变排除了中间跨视相互作用. 为了克服这些限制,我们提议ReMOT,一个“转换器”启发式框架,从空间一致的RGB和完全被冻结的视觉基础上的波浪观点读取补充知识。 ReMOT利用了阶段性的联合关注来使受控的局部和全球交叉视图互动成为可能,而可学习的聚变查询则在不回写的情况下逐渐读取跨变形器深度的补充证据. blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The rapid evolution of image generation poses a fundamental
challenge to AI-generated image detection: generalizing
beyond the generators encountered during training.
Detectors must recognize unseen synthesis methods [ 37 ] while
remaining robust to variations in image content, source
distributions, and post-processing [ 17 ] .
Yet learned forensic cues [ 35 , 30 , 38 ] may capture generator-specific artifacts or dataset
biases rather than transferable evidence of synthesis [ 47 , 5 , 25 , 12 ] . UnivFD [ 23 ] provided early evidence of the potential of pretrained
visual knowledge, demonstrating transferable detection
using frozen CLIP [ 26 ] representations
and simple classifiers. Motivated by this potential,
considerable research has focused on adapting pretrained
backbones to improve cross-generator generalization.
Methods such as FatFormer [ 21 ] and Effort [ 40 ] modify pretrained feature processing for detection while seeking
to preserve transferable visual knowledge.

blocks.en:
Recent findings, however, challenge whether such
adaptation is always necessary. Simplicity Prevails [ 45 ] demonstrates that modern
vision foundation models (VFMs), particularly DINOv3 [ 27 ] , already encode highly
transferable detection knowledge accessible through
simple linear probing. Moreover, additional adaptation,
including LoRA [ 14 ] , can substantially
degrade generalization in its evaluated settings.
These findings motivate a shift in emphasis from backbone adaptation to knowledge readout .
Yet how to effectively exploit this knowledge remains
underexplored. Conventional frozen linear probing
typically relies on a single final-layer RGB
representation, leaving complementary evidence across
views and Transformer depth largely unexploited.
Meanwhile, multi-cue detectors incorporate semantic,
spatial, and frequency-related evidence, but representative
approaches often involve adaptation, heterogeneous
encoding, and late fusion [ 39 , 6 ] .
These designs entail distinct tradeoffs: adaptation
may favor training-specific patterns; heterogeneous
encoders produce representations with different
inductive biases and abstraction levels, complicating
their integration; and late fusion prevents intermediate
interaction between independently encoded views.
This leaves a fundamental question: how can frozen encoders with the same architecture
jointly exploit complementary forensic evidence beyond
final-layer RGB probing?

blocks.en:
Our central insight is that organizing complementary evidence
and learning how to read it can better exploit pretrained detection
knowledge without learning task-specific visual transformations .
Complementary views can interact
within a common pretrained architecture, while their evidence
can be accessed throughout feature extraction. Cross-view interaction
and readout determine how this knowledge is accessed.
Effective readout therefore involves both cross-view organization
and access across Transformer depth.
We realize this perspective in ReMoT ( Re adout with M ixture- o f- T ransformers),
a framework for progressive cross-view readout in
AI-generated image detection.
MoT [ 20 ] combines modality-specific
Transformer parameters with joint attention across modalities.
ReMoT adopts this principle for spatially aligned RGB
and discrete wavelet transform (DWT) views. Both streams use
the same frozen DINOv3 architecture and pretrained weights, providing a common foundation
for MoT-inspired joint attention.
A staged joint-attention mechanism initially
preserves view-specific processing and subsequently
enables controlled cross-view interaction through
local patch correspondence and global register-mediated
communication. Meanwhile, learnable fusion queries progressively read both views across Transformer
depth using frozen attention projections, without
writing back to view tokens. Together, these mechanisms organize
cross-view evidence for progressive readout while preserving
pretrained backbone weights. Trained solely
on GenImage Stable Diffusion v1.4 (SD v1.4), ReMoT achieves 91.2% average accuracy across eight
benchmark groups (Figure 1 ) with only 3,074 trainable
parameters in its equivalent implementation,
attaining the highest overall average among the
evaluated methods. An independently trained variant without
direct cross-view interaction reaches 87.0%, highlighting the
value of evidence exchange alongside progressive query readout.

Our contributions are summarized as follows: 1. We advance a readout-centered perspective for generalizable detection, shifting
the design focus from adapting pretrained representations
to organizing and accessing their existing detection knowledge. 2. We propose ReMoT , combining frozen RGB/DWT

and global register exchange, and learnable fusion queries
for progressive readout across depth without writing back
to either visual stream. 3. ReMoT achieves a leading 91.2% average accuracy across eight benchmark groups, outperforming prior
adaptation-based detectors and showing the potential of knowledge readout for generalizable detection.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 From adaptation to readout
blocks.zh: 2.1 从适应到读出

blocks.en:
Generator-specific artifacts and dataset biases limit
cross-generator detection [ 5 , 12 ] .
UnivFD [ 23 ] demonstrated the value of
pretrained knowledge through simple classifiers on frozen
CLIP [ 26 ] features. Self-supervised
foundations offer another source of transferable visual
features [ 24 ] . Subsequent adaptation
methods seek stronger detection representations while
preserving transferability: FatFormer [ 21 ] introduces
forgery-aware transformations, and Effort [ 40 ] learns in an orthogonal subspace while freezing principal
pretrained components. Prompt-based methods likewise adapt
pretrained representations for detection [ 32 , 36 ] .
OmniAID [ 13 ] decouples content-dependent
semantic flaws from universal artifacts through routable
semantic experts and an always-active artifact expert.
Complementary reconstruction-based training improves cross-generator
generalization [ 4 , 29 ] ; DDA [ 5 ] aligns real and synthetic images in pixel and frequency
domains to suppress spurious correlations.
Recent evidence questions whether further adaptation is
necessary. Simplicity Prevails [ 45 ] finds that modern VFMs, including DINOv3 [ 27 ] ,
already support strong generalization through linear probing,
while additional adaptation can degrade performance in its
evaluated settings. These findings motivate readout beyond
final-layer probing: ReMoT explores how existing visual knowledge
can be accessed across views and depth while backbone weights remain frozen.

blocks.en: 2.2 Cross-view evidence integration
blocks.zh: 2.2 交叉观点证据整合

blocks.en:
Beyond final-layer RGB probing, complementary evidence can be
sought across image views and Transformer depth.
Local artifact modeling [ 31 , 19 , 44 , 34 ] ,
reconstruction [ 7 ] , and quantization cues [ 42 ] complement RGB appearance.
Spectral analyses caution against universal fingerprints [ 3 , 10 ] , motivating
robust spectral representations [ 15 , 18 , 16 ] .
Layer Consistency Matters [ 41 ] identifies evidence
in latent transitions across layers. Multi-cue detectors and
multimodal reasoning [ 46 ] explore evidence integration:
AIDE [ 39 ] integrates semantic features with
forensic features from texture-selected patches, while
CO-SPY [ 6 ] enhances and adaptively fuses
semantic and pixel-level features. However, heterogeneous
encoders complicate feature alignment, and late fusion limits
exchange during feature extraction. Developed for multimodal
pretraining, MoT [ 20 ] combines trainable
modality-specific Transformer parameters with joint self-attention.
ReMoT borrows this joint-processing principle to exchange and
progressively read spatially aligned RGB and wavelet
evidence [ 22 ] using frozen pretrained backbones.

blocks.en:

foundation through MoT-inspired joint processing, staged cross-view
interaction, and progressive query readout (Figure 3 ).
The two views share a joint attention space, with a stage-dependent mask
governing their interaction. Learnable queries collect evidence
across Transformer depth while pretrained backbone weights remain frozen.

blocks.en:
Broad cross-benchmark transfer. ReMoT ranks first on five
groups and second on three, averaging 91.2% (Table 1 ). Mirage-Test exposes severe transfer
failures among baselines, with even the strongest reaching only
55.7%, versus ReMoT’s 84.1%. The lead also holds across the other

90.1%. Transfer also spans unseen generators in GI-QF96/AIGCB-QF96
(Tables 2 and 3 ) and nonphotographic
Anime images in Mirage-Test (84.83%). Together, these results show
that ReMoT’s overall advantage is sustained across diverse benchmarks
rather than driven by an isolated gain on a single dataset.

blocks.en: 4.3 Ablation studies
blocks.zh: 4.3 读取研究

blocks.en:
The ablations support learning to read frozen features and combining
complementary views through selective interaction
(Table 6 ). ReMoT reaches 91.2% average accuracy,
compared with 84.2% for final-layer RGB linear probing.
Adding modality-specific attention LoRA ( r = 8 r=8 , α = 16 \alpha=16 )
increases trainable parameters to approximately 2.37M but lowers
accuracy to 70.5%. This comparison supports learning to read
pretrained features rather than learning task-specific feature transformations.
For the input views, RGB-only and DWT-only
query readouts achieve 86.6% and 68.0%: RGB provides the stronger
individual evidence, while combining both yields the best average.
Retaining fusion-query readout while disabling cross-view attention
( s = 24 s=24 ) yields 87.0%,
4.2 points below ReMoT.
ReMoT improves seven of eight groups, most notably SynthWildX
(+7.1 points) and WildRF (+11.3); EvalGEN scores are 96.3%
and 98.0%, respectively.
The mask variants then examine how views should communicate:
local patch attention alone and global register attention alone
reach 89.6% and 89.1%, versus 91.2% with both. Both ablations
preserve within-view attention and query readout, supporting complementary local
correspondence and global communication. Making patch attention
global instead yields 90.5%, with lower scores on all eight groups
despite retaining global register communication. These results
favor spatially selective patch exchange alongside global register
communication. Among mask variants, local-only leads on GI-QF96 and EvalGEN, and

blocks.en:
We proposed ReMoT to address transfer risks from backbone adaptation
and the limited scope of existing readout approaches.
It couples staged cross-view interaction with progressive evidence
collection across Transformer depth, while keeping pretrained
backbone weights frozen. Trained on a single generator, ReMoT
achieves broad cross-benchmark generalization,
balanced predictions, and strong robustness
to image post-processing. These findings motivate a research focus
on readout design: organizing complementary evidence and learning
how to access pretrained knowledge provide an effective basis for
generalization across unfamiliar generators and diverse image sources.

blocks.en:
ReMoT’s MoT-inspired formulation assigns separate Transformer
parameter slots to the RGB and DWT streams and uses K K fusion
queries for progressive readout. Under our training setup, we find
that ReMoT admits a more compact, exactly equivalent implementation.
It shares the slot weights and replaces the K K queries with one
query and a fixed attention bias, preserving both visual streams,
their staged interaction, and the model’s predictions.
Weight sharing relies on identical slot
parameters, which we maintain by freezing both slots at the same
pretrained initialization. Query reduction relies on identical
initial query states and symmetric computation at every layer.
Modality-specific updates that make the slot weights differ or
query-specific changes that break symmetry invalidate the
respective equivalence.
